title: Tiny Journey Blueprints — personal lab journal
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a personal scratchpad for a small feature set I want to prototype: compact, composable session templates called "Tiny Journeys". The goal is to give product teams a fast way to scaffold common multi-turn patterns (concise assistant, guided Q/A, checklist-style follow-ups) with explicit token budgets and optional cheap fallbacks.

Why (problem):
- Customers keep asking for out-of-the-box session starters (for search assistants, customer support, note-taking) that are smaller than full persona systems but still structured.
- Building full custom prompts is heavy for non-ML teams; we can offer short templates that are safe and cost-aware.
- Need to reduce repeated token overhead for common flows and make it easy to A/B different compact strategies.

Proposed feature (high level):
- A library of 3–5 Tiny Journey templates available via API + Console.
- Each template has: name, description, tokens_budget (soft), compression_hint (e.g., prefer summary vs full context), fallback_model (cheaper model id), telemetry tags.
- Console UI: pick a template, adjust budget sliders, preview sample exchange, save as route preset.

Core templates to prototype (first pass):
1) Concise Assistant (CA): short system instruction, strict token cap, prefer short answers + bullet lists.
2) Guided Q/A (GQA): asks clarifying question(s) if query ambiguous, limits back-and-forth to 2 clarifications, then final answer.
3) Checklist Coach (CC): breaks task into 3 steps, returns prioritized checklist with estimated completion times.

User stories (examples):
- As a PM, I want a "Concise Assistant" preset that reduces average tokens per session by ~40% while preserving >85% task completion in guided tests.
- As a developer, I want an API flag template_id=concise-assistant so I can wire it into my support bot with one config change.
- As an analyst, I want telemetry that shows tokens saved vs baseline route for every session so I can compute cost delta.

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- API: /v1/sessions supports template_id field; template controls system prompt + token_budget + fallback_model.
- Console: preset editor shows slider for token_budget and preview for one sample user input.
- Backend: if token_budget would be exceeded, automatically route to fallback_model or emit condensed prompt attempt (configurable).
- Metric: average tokens/session for routes using a Tiny Journey must be reduced by >=25% in the first internal test vs current baseline.

Telemetry / metrics to collect:
- tokens_requested, tokens_consumed, model_used_primary, model_used_fallback, latency_p95, user_satisfaction_probe (one-question survey: was result helpful?), conversion (task complete boolean).
- Derived: tokens_saved_pct, cost_delta_usd, fallback_rate.

Experiment design / rollout plan:
- Stage 0: internal dogfood on 2 internal apps (search-bot, notes helper) for 2 weeks. Manual QA of safety and hallucination for Concise Assistant.
- Stage 1: soft-launch to 10% of eligible traffic behind feature flag, compare metrics to control for 14 days.
- Stage 2: expand to 50% if fallback_rate < 8% and user_satisfaction_drop < 3%.

Implementation notes (engineering thoughts):
- API shape: session_create payload gets optional template_id + overrides object { token_budget, fallback_model }. Template expands to system prompt + assistant behavior hints.
- Runtime: make template expansion part of the request preprocessing; add token accounting check BEFORE dispatching to heavy model. If potential overflow, call short-form compressor routine (prefix-only summary) or switch to fallback_model.
- Caching: templates could include static prefix that is cached in KV to reduce repeated compute.

UI sketch (console):
- Templates list with cards: name, short blurb, expected token range, cost estimate per 1k requests.
- Edit mode: slider for token budget, toggle for fallback model, test sample input box, preview response.

Safety & QA checklist:
- Ensure template system prompts don't encourage disallowed content; add static guard layer that rejects risky system text during template creation.
- Run micro-evals comparing hallucination rate for CA vs standard full prompt.

Open questions / items to decide:
- What is default token_budget for each template? (CA: 150 tokens? GQA: 250?) Need bench results.
- How aggressive should automated condensation be vs switching to fallback? Who decides? global policy vs per-template?
- Do we expose template editing to non-admins in Console? Probably not initially.
- How to version templates for customers who pin routes? Include template_version field.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: overly aggressive truncation reduces quality -> mitigate with canary and conservative defaults, fail-open to fallback model.
- Risk: revenue impact if too many fallbacks route to expensive models -> need cost guardrails and budget hard-limits.

Quick TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Run token budget sweep on CA/GQA/CC against 3 representative queries (support, doc search, to-do capture). (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Draft API proposal for template_id and overrides; PR skeleton. (owner: Jasper)
- [ ] Mockup console cards and slider UI. (owner: Ava)
- [ ] Create micro-eval suite for hallucination & helpfulness. (owner: Noah)

Notes to self: keep this lightweight; the point is to make a low-friction entry-point for teams to try structure without committing to full persona engineering. Keep templates composable — e.g., allow "post-process: summary-or-expand" hook so apps can opt into a one-line recap.

Example sample (Concise Assistant):
- System: "You are a helpful assistant. Keep answers under 3 sentences and use bullet lists when possible. If you need to ask a clarifying question, ask one short question."
- token_budget: 150
- fallback_model: rwinf-small-1

Sample API usage (pseudocode):
POST /v1/sessions
{
  "template_id": "concise-assistant",
  "overrides": { "token_budget": 120 },
  "input": "How do I reset my API key in the console?"
}

Longer-term possibilities (brain-dump):
- Marketplace of Tiny Journeys maintained by Redwood + community-contributed templates (with review flow).
- Template composition e.g., chain CA -> CC for multi-step tasks.
- Automatic template suggestion: runtime detects high token users and suggests switching to a compact template.

References / inspiration:
- internal: thread #tiny-journeys (Slack) + INF-4279 spec stub
- external: small prompt patterns from community note templates, checklist UX from productivity apps

End of jot — will flesh into a PRD skeleton once initial token sweep results are in.
